newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana Airways keeps options open on damaged plane.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Airways keeps options open on damaged plane.

text.p: Ghana Airways has yet to decide how to replace the McDonnell Douglas DC-9-51 airliner that ensured its service along the coast of West Africa until it crash-landed at Ivory Coast's Abidjan airport on April 12, a top official said on Monday.
"We are waiting for the report by the insurance company. It is their decision whether the plane will be repaired or not," the airline's commercial director John Kirby told Reuters.
"We are in the middle of negotiations. We have a number of negotiations on the go. It would be premature to say whether we are going to buy or to lease another plane," he added.
The airline said on Friday it hoped to resume its west coast service, a major source of revenue with an average passenger loadfactor of 59 percent in 1996, by the end of May.

The damaged DC-9 is 19 years old and wholly-owned by Ghana Airways. The airline wholly owns one other plane, a 15-year old DC-10-30, and leases a 23-year second old DC-10-30 from Brussels-based Skyjet. Both planes fly on South and East Africa and intercontinental routes.

Kirby and Chief Executive Rex Lezard are from wholly owned British Airways Speedwing Consulting Ltd, which won a two-year management contract in July 1995 to prepare Ghana Airways for privatisation. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
